A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TaDSE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and the relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original intent-classification experiments across five datasets, augmentation and loss ablations, semantic-compression tests, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B evaluation results on SNIPS and ATIS in Table 6.

M1.justification: The template augmentation procedure, three contrastive losses, optional template MLP and semantic-compression inference remain unchanged in Section 3 and Equations (1)–(5).

E1.justification: Both versions use SNIPS, ATIS, MASSIVE, HWU64 and CLINC150 for English dialogue intent classification. The added Qwen comparison uses the already evaluated SNIPS and ATIS scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B to the comparison moved from v2 Appendix E, Table 12, to Section 5.5, Table 6. Both OpenAI models and Gemini remain participants under shortened table labels; the dialogue-baseline comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the reported test sizes, kNN evaluation, training budgets, hyperparameters and validation-based compression selection. The relocated embedding comparison retains 768-dimensional representations; no separate protocol change accompanies the added comparator.

E4.justification: The augmentation and loss ablations, semantic-compression tests, kNN sensitivity, training-stability curves and representation-space analyses are retained. The ATIS utterance examples are relocated unchanged; Section 5.5 adds interpretation without a new mechanism test.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies and the same plots without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3 adds no statistical or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 Table 6 adds Qwen3-0.6B accuracies of 92.14 on SNIPS, 89.14 on ATIS and 90.64 on average. All four rows inherited from v2 Table 12 are numerically unchanged, including TaDSE's 97.00, 89.70 and 93.35. The other tables and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including the contrastive objectives, compression formula and uniformity/alignment definitions, are unchanged. The definitions move from Appendix F to Appendix E without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning template augmentation, pairwise learning, dialogue embedding performance and semantic compression. The third introductory contribution is reworded without changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 expands v2's conjecture about complicated ATIS sentences into an explanation involving compositional templates, SNIPS/ATIS differences and augmentation order. It additionally suggests structural priors can substitute for supervised training data and model capacity. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code upon acceptance with a code-availability statement and repository URL. Appendix C's implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and evaluation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Gemini embedding by Lee et al. (2025) and Qwen3 embedding by Zhang et al. (2025), extending the existing commercial-embedding discussion to an open-source comparator. The related-work section and core novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The short Appendix E comparison becomes an expanded Section 5.5, with corresponding cross-reference and appendix-letter changes. v3 also corrects contribution-list wording and updates affiliation/contact text. Most prose and section ordering are retained.

P2.justification: Former Table 12 becomes a reformatted single-column Table 6 in the main text, with shorter model labels, an added Qwen row and a revised caption. All eleven figures are retained, with limited placement and appendix-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added open-source comparator and concrete repository URL modestly improve comparative context and reproducibility information. Moving the existing comparison into Section 5.5 also makes it easier to assess. The broader claims about substituting for supervision and model capacity lack new controlled evidence, limiting the benefit of the expanded interpretation.
